title: The screen brief checklist
subtitle: What we need from your media owner before we build, so your film is accepted first time.
intro: Most delays on a 3D campaign come from missing information about the screen, not from the creative. Send this list to your media owner, or to us, and the production starts on solid ground.

sections.title: The screen
items: Media owner and site name
Address and screen reference
Shape: portrait, landscape, corner or facade
Real size of the screen and how far people stand from it

sections.title: The exact layout
items: Resolution of each face
Gaps and edges between faces
The angle, if it is a corner screen
Areas that must stay clear
The template file the media owner provides

sections.title: The video format accepted
items: File type and maximum size
Frames per second
Length of the spot and how often it plays
Sound or no sound
Anything about colour or brightness

sections.title: The view people have
items: A photo or video from where people usually see the screen
How far and how high that spot is
Poles, trees, signs or reflections in the way
What it looks like by day and by night

sections.title: The schedule
items: Campaign dates and share of the loop
Delivery deadline and approval time
Who signs off on the media-owner side
A test slot on the real screen, if possible

sections.title: The delivery
items: How files should be named
Where and how to send them
The other screens in the network that need a version
A still image for screens that refuse video

closing: Missing half of it? That is normal. Send what you have and we ask the media owner for the rest.
